stem: If A = {x : x is a prime number less than 10} and B = {x : x is an odd number less than 10}, which of the following correctly describes A minus B (i.e., elements in A but not in B)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: A = {2,3,5,7}, B = {1,3,5,7,9}. A minus B removes elements common to both: {3,5,7}. Only 2 remains.
This is A intersect B = {3,5,7}, confusing set difference with intersection.
This returns A itself = {2,3,5,7}, failing to subtract elements that are also in B.
This is B = {1,3,5,7,9}, confusing A minus B with B itself.

explanation: A = {2,3,5,7} (primes below 10). B = {1,3,5,7,9} (odd numbers below 10). A minus B = A \ B = elements in A that are not in B = {2}, since 3, 5, 7 are in both.

explanation_sections.punchline: A minus B keeps only what A has that B does not: since every odd prime stays in B, only the even prime 2 survives.
explanation_sections.approach: State the definition: A \ B = {x in A : x not in B}. List A, then cross out anything that also appears in B.
explanation_sections.lesson: Set difference A \ B is NOT the same as A intersect B; it retains elements exclusive to A.
explanation_sections.timing: 50 s. The trap is option 2 ({3,5,7}), which is the intersection of A and B.
